title: Injective acyclicity gives bounded-below base change (Lean split, general coefficients)
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Call a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] *torsion* if its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Throughout, sheaves and complexes of $\Lambda$-modules are regarded as abelian sheaves and complexes of abelian sheaves through the forgetful functor, and the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], (higher) direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] are those of abelian sheaves. Assume coefficient-wise injective acyclicity: for every prime $\ell$, every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with induced $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and every injective sheaf $I$ of $(\Lambda/\ell)_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, one has $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for all $q>0$ (higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] of the underlying abelian sheaf). Then for every such square and every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ all of whose cohomology sheaves are torsion, represented by a bounded below complex of $\Lambda_X$-modules and regarded as an object of $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$. No hypothesis is put on $g$.

proof.text: The degree-zero case is the arbitrary-coefficient torsion-sheaf dévissage: under coefficient-wise injective acyclicity (the hypothesis of this lemma), for every cartesian square and torsion $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf $F$, the derived exchange $\Ex_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$. (The hypothesis of this lemma is exactly that of the cited node.)

Choose a bounded-below representative of $K$ and the canonical truncation triangles. Applying $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ produces truncation exact couples and spectral sequences; exactness of inverse image identifies the second graded term with $R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$, and naturality of derived exchange gives a morphism between the couples.
Every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is torsion, so Step 1 identifies the morphism on every $E_2$-term as an isomorphism.

proof.text: Induction on the page number preserves the isomorphism because $E_{r+1}$ is the cohomology of $(E_r,d_r)$ and the morphism commutes with $d_r$. Bounded-below convergence gives finite exhaustive separated filtrations on each total-degree abutment, with $E_\infty$ as associated graded.

source.place: Lemma 0DDE, proof of convergence and page induction

proof.text: The exchange map on the abutments respects the finite filtrations and induces the $E_\infty$ isomorphisms on their graded pieces. Finite-filtration induction therefore makes each cohomology map $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 0DDE, proof of the abutment filtration

proof.text: A morphism in the bounded-below derived category whose cohomology sheaf maps are all isomorphisms is an isomorphism, so $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.
